counterfactual_missing_items: asymptomatic irreversible pulpitis with normal apical tissues
radiographs showed generalized alveolar bone loss consistent with stage II, grade II periodontitis
decisive_items: Cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth #11 and #21, originating from the external palatal surface and perforating into the pulp space
Periapical radiographs of the maxillary central incisors revealed cervical areas of rarefaction
The diagnosis for both central incisors was asymptomatic irreversible pulpitis with normal apical tissues and external cervical resorption
response.rationale: C1 is the most specific primary lesional diagnosis: CBCT localizes cervical resorption to the palatal aspects of #11/#21, with external origin and pulp perforation; the unchanged canal outline and cervical rarefaction favor external cervical resorption. The final diagnosis names ECR alongside pulpitis, indicating that pulpitis is a downstream complication rather than the primary diagnosis. C2 captures the co-named pulpitis but omits the causative resorptive lesion; R1/C3 only capture the separate generalized periodontitis; R4 is correct but less anatomically complete than C1.

rejected.why: Only describes generalized periodontitis and does not explain the localized palatal resorptive lesions or CBCT findings.
Same periodontitis limitation; generalized modifier does not address the incisor-specific cervical resorption or pulp involvement.
Pulpitis is named in the final diagnosis but is a downstream consequence of external cervical resorption; label omits the CBCT-verified resorptive lesion.
Correct diagnosis but less complete than C1 because it lacks the exact teeth and palatal distribution supported by the CBCT span.
